summary: An interior page of The Anaconda Standard for 23 July 1890, densely typeset across six columns with a mix of local mining news, legal notices, financial tables, and large display advertising. The left portion of the page is editorial — mining and prospects reports, mining stock exchange prices, bonds and stocks tables, and the sump recovery story — while the right third is dominated by large display advertisements for Estes & Connell Mercantile Company's summer sale and the Tuttle Manufacturing and Supply Co. The editorial tone is matter-of-fact and commercial, treating a grim mine-shaft body recovery with the same column weight as ore-strike reports and stock quotations.
headlines: The Bodies of Murphy and Kelleher Recovered at Last

clipping_placements.placement_note: top of column, banner headline spanning full column width, directly adjacent to Mining Stock Exchange table to its left

juxtapositions: The Murphy and Kelleher sump-recovery story — bodies identified only by clothing after eight months — sits immediately to the right of the Mining Stock Exchange price listings, placing a grim human toll of mine labour in direct visual proximity to commodity valuations of mining shares.

A large, festive Estes & Connell advertisement promoting a Saturday sale on children's clothing occupies the right-hand columns on the same page as the account of two miners' decomposed bodies being lifted from a shaft.
